rendered: The strain is R82, an osmotic-stress–tolerant derivative of SDSPY-136 → R82[1], reported in the section on prodigiosin production. How it was obtained: adaptive laboratory evolution, in which the parent strain was propagated for 120 generations under high osmotic pressure[2] to select for tolerance; the listed strategy is Adaptive laboratory evolution for improved osmotic tolerance[3]. Transcriptomic analysis of the evolved strain showed global reprogramming of 830 genes that optimized[4] precursor supply and product release. Fermentation scale: In 5 L fed-batch fermentation, R82 reached 11.4 g[5]L^(cid:0) 1 prodigiosin (~double the original strain)[6]. Note that the summary table lists the same titer with a different cultivation descriptor and time, namely 11,400[7] (in the units of its header, (mg L^(cid:0) 1)[8]) obtained in shake flask[9] mode over 48[10] h, so the scale entry in Table 2[11] differs from the main text.
